import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Set style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-darkgrid')
sns.set_palette("husl")

# Create the dataset
data = {
    'brand': ['Leica', 'Fuji', 'Pentax', 'Olympus', 'Leica'],
    'model_year': [2005, 2019, 2012, 2015, 2016],
    'megapixels': [13.5, 46.4, 38.7, 22.5, 12.2],
    'max_iso': [25600, 51200, 12800, 6400, 25600],
    'weight_grams': [324, 1151, 598, 1095, 290],
    'price_usd': [811.8, 3596.41, 3357.2, 1555.7, 3899.09],
    'sensor_type': ['Micro 4/3', 'APS-C', 'Full Frame', 'APS-C', 'Medium Format'],
    'has_video_4k': [1, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    'lens_mount': ['E', 'EF', 'MFT', 'Z', 'MFT'],
    'body_type': ['Compact', 'Mirrorless', 'Mirrorless', 'Mirrorless', 'DSLR']
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Create figure with subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(20, 16))

# 1. Scatter plot: Price vs Megapixels with sensor type
ax1 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 1)
scatter = ax1.scatter(df['megapixels'], df['price_usd'], 
                      c=df['model_year'], s=df['weight_grams']/10, 
                      alpha=0.7, cmap='viridis')
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels')
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)')
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels (size=weight, color=year)')
plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax1, label='Model Year')

# Add brand labels
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    ax1.annotate(row['brand'], (row['megapixels'], row['price_usd']), 
                xytext=(5, 5), textcoords='offset points', fontsize=9)

# 2. Bar plot: Average price by brand
ax2 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 2)
brand_price = df.groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
bars = ax2.bar(brand_price.index, brand_price.values)
ax2.set_xlabel('Brand')
ax2.set_ylabel('Average Price (USD)')
ax2.set_title('Average Price by Brand')
ax2.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Add value labels on bars
for bar in bars:
    height = bar.get_height()
    ax2.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 50,
             f'${height:,.0f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)

# 3. Box plot: Price distribution by body type
ax3 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 3)
df['has_video_4k_str'] = df['has_video_4k'].map({1: '4K Video', 0: 'No 4K Video'})
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='body_type', y='price_usd', hue='has_video_4k_str', ax=ax3)
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type')
ax3.set_ylabel('Price (USD)')
ax3.set_title('Price Distribution by Body Type & 4K Video')
ax3.legend(title='4K Video')
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 4. Line plot: Camera specs over years
ax4 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 4)
ax4.plot(df['model_year'], df['megapixels'], 'o-', label='Megapixels', linewidth=2)
ax4.plot(df['model_year'], df['max_iso']/1000, 's-', label='Max ISO (thousands)', linewidth=2)
ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year')
ax4.set_ylabel('Value')
ax4.set_title('Camera Specs Over Years')
ax4.legend()
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Add brand labels to points
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    ax4.annotate(row['brand'], (row['model_year'], row['megapixels']), 
                xytext=(5, 5), textcoords='offset points', fontsize=8)

# 5. Pie chart: Distribution of sensor types
ax5 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 5)
sensor_counts = df['sensor_type'].value_counts()
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax5.pie(sensor_counts.values, labels=sensor_counts.index,
                                   autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90)
ax5.set_title('Distribution of Sensor Types')
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')

# 6. Heatmap: Correlation matrix
ax6 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 6)
numeric_cols = ['model_year', 'megapixels', 'max_iso', 'weight_grams', 'price_usd']
corr_matrix = df[numeric_cols].corr()
im = ax6.imshow(corr_matrix, cmap='coolwarm', vmin=-1, vmax=1)
ax6.set_xticks(range(len(numeric_cols)))
ax6.set_yticks(range(len(numeric_cols)))
ax6.set_xticklabels(numeric_cols, rotation=45, ha='right')
ax6.set_yticklabels(numeric_cols)
ax6.set_title('Correlation Matrix')

# Add correlation values
for i in range(len(numeric_cols)):
    for j in range(len(numeric_cols)):
        text = ax6.text(j, i, f'{corr_matrix.iloc[i, j]:.2f}',
                       ha="center", va="center", color="white", fontsize=9)

# 7. Violin plot: Weight distribution by body type
ax7 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 7)
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='body_type', y='weight_grams', ax=ax7)
ax7.set_xlabel('Body Type')
ax7.set_ylabel('Weight (grams)')
ax7.set_title('Weight Distribution by Body Type')
ax7.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 8. Stacked bar: Features by brand
ax8 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 8)
features_df = df[['brand', 'has_video_4k']].copy()
features_df['has_video_4k'] = features_df['has_video_4k'].map({1: '4K', 0: 'No 4K'})
feature_counts = pd.crosstab(features_df['brand'], features_df['has_video_4k'])
feature_counts.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=ax8)
ax8.set_xlabel('Brand')
ax8.set_ylabel('Count')
ax8.set_title('4K Video Capability by Brand')
ax8.legend(title='4K Video')
ax8.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 9. Radar chart for camera comparison
ax9 = plt.subplot(3, 3, 9, projection='polar')

# Normalize data for radar chart
numeric_features = ['megapixels', 'max_iso', 'weight_grams', 'price_usd']
normalized_df = df[numeric_features].copy()
for col in numeric_features:
    normalized_df[col] = (normalized_df[col] - normalized_df[col].min()) / (normalized_df[col].max() - normalized_df[col].min())

# Prepare angles
angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, len(numeric_features), endpoint=False).tolist()
angles += angles[:1]  # Close the polygon

# Plot each camera
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    values = normalized_df.iloc[idx].values.tolist()
    values += values[:1]  # Close the polygon
    ax9.plot(angles, values, 'o-', linewidth=2, label=row['brand'])
    ax9.fill(angles, values, alpha=0.1)

ax9.set_xticks(angles[:-1])

ax9.set_ylim(0, 1)
